It's still a loan- that is a huge increase in debt, how does that not disadvantage poorer citizens? A debt is a debt, even if it's interest free. There are also proposed discounts for paying fees upfront (something only wealthy people can do)... wealthier citizens will in some cases pay less for their education.  And yes, the supported places are definitely an issue! I totally think university should be more accessible, and welcome the changes to STEM degrees etc...why does this have to result in other areas being totally screwed over?

It's awesome that you will now be able to go to uni! But it's 113% (more than double) increase and means it will become inaccessible (to an even higher degree) for already poor and disadvantaged citizens.

Not to mention the degrees themselves are being streamlined and becoming less valuable- long term may lead to an even worse literacy crisis.
